title: Digital customer experience: Strategy, journey, and metrics
summary: Define digital customer experience, map it across the whole customer journey, and measure the touchpoints that decide whether your customers stay or go.
body_markdown:
***How to map digital customer experience across the customer journey and measure it at every touchpoint.***


You’ve added more digital touchpoints in the past two years than in the decade before: a mobile app, live chat, a help center, messaging, maybe a chatbot. Each one met a real need. What’s harder is seeing them as a single experience, so when a customer disengages, the point of failure is difficult to identify.


That’s the gap most customer experience and operations teams live with. Each channel launched on its own, the data sits in separate systems, and nobody sees the customer’s path from end to end. The experience a customer gets depends on where they reach first.


Getting it back under control starts with the fundamentals. You need a shared definition of digital customer experience, a map of the journey it runs across, stage-level metrics, and an owner for the touchpoints that break.


This guide is built around that work. It provides the two things most teams are missing: a stage-by-stage journey map, and a metric for each stage, so you can measure digital customer experience and act on it.


## Key takeaways


- Digital customer experience is every interaction a customer has across your digital channels
- Customer engagement measures the brand’s outreach; digital customer experience measures the customer’s perception
- A stage-by-stage journey map turns a vague experience into measurable moments
- Core metrics tied to each journey stage make the experience trackable
- The biggest gains come from fixing your highest-friction touchpoints first


## What is digital customer experience?


Digital customer experience is the sum of how a customer perceives every interaction with your brand across digital channels, from your website and mobile app to live chat, email, self-service, and social media. It’s the customer’s view of those touchpoints, shaped by how consistent and connected each step feels as they move from one channel to the next.


In practice, it’s what the experience looks like from the customer’s side of the screen. Someone who starts in your help center, moves to live chat, and finishes in your mobile app forms one impression, even when your teams see three separate systems behind it. That impression is what shapes whether they come back, and it forms across channels your teams run separately.


It’s also a broader concept. While user experience focuses on how one screen or app behaves, digital customer experience covers the whole chain of digital moments a customer strings together to get something done.


### Digital customer experience vs. customer engagement


**Digital customer experience** is the customer’s perception of your brand across touchpoints, while **customer engagement** is the outreach you do to prompt interaction. One measures how the experience lands, and the other measures how often and how well you reach out. Engagement is one input you control; experience is the outcome you measure.


A push notification about an abandoned cart is engagement, since you’re the one initiating the contact. How that customer feels when they tap through and complete the purchase is experience, shaped entirely by their perception of that moment.


The two aren’t interchangeable, and no volume of outreach will fix a checkout that loses people at the payment step.


## The digital customer experience journey: A stage-by-stage framework


This is the part many teams skip, and it’s where digital customer experience becomes measurable. Map customer experience to the customer journey, and a vague idea turns into a set of moments you can track.


Most B2C experiences compress into four or five stages: discovery, purchase, delivery or first use, support, and repeat or referral.


**B2C journey stage** **Digital touchpoints** **What to measure**


**Discovery** Search, social, ads, brand site, review sites Traffic, click-through rate, bounce rate


**Consideration** Product pages, ratings and reviews, chat, chatbot Add-to-cart rate, chat engagement, product-page dwell


**Purchase** Cart, checkout, mobile app, payment Conversion rate, cart abandonment, checkout time


**Delivery and first use** Order tracking, confirmation email and SMS, app setup On-time delivery, activation rate, time to first use


**Support** Self-service help center, chatbot, live chat, social DMs First-contact resolution, CSAT, digital containment


**Loyalty and advocacy** Loyalty program, email, app notifications, referrals Repeat-purchase rate, NPS, referral rate


The B2C journey is shorter and higher-volume than B2B, which usually runs across five to seven stages, so a single weak touchpoint shows up fast in reviews and repeat-purchase rates.


**B2B journey stage** **Digital touchpoints** **What to measure**


**Awareness** Website, search, social, review sites Traffic, bounce rate, time on page


**Consideration** Product pages, live chat, demos, email Chat response time, content engagement


**Purchase** Checkout, forms, self-service signup Conversion rate, form abandonment


**Onboarding** Welcome emails, in-app guidance, help center Activation rate, time to first value


**Support** Live chat, chatbot, self-service, ticketing First-contact resolution, satisfaction, digital containment


**Retention** Account portal, renewal reminders, status updates Churn rate, loyalty score


**Advocacy** Referral programs, reviews, community Referral rate, review volume


A good experience looks different at each stage. In support it means a customer resolves an issue in one channel without repeating themselves, and in onboarding it means reaching first value without needing a human handoff. When those stages share one view of the customer, the result is an[omnichannel contact center](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/what-is-an-omnichannel-cloud-contact-center/) : one continuous record of the journey across every channel.


## How to measure digital customer experience


Measure digital customer experience with a set of five metrics tied to the journey stages:


- **[Customer satisfaction](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/customer-satisfaction-everything-you-need-to-know/) (CSAT):** a short post-interaction score telling you whether a specific touchpoint met expectations. Trigger it right after a chat or a self-service session, and act on it by rebuilding the lowest-scoring touchpoints first.
- **[Net Promoter Score](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/nps-in-your-customer-care-strategy/) (NPS):** a relationship-level measure of whether customers would recommend you. Read it quarterly, and treat a falling score as an early signal of experience problems before churn shows up in revenue.
- **[Customer Effort Score](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/key-factors-impacting-customer-effort-score/) (CES):** how hard a customer had to work to get something done. Capture it at the end of a task, and target the steps where effort spikes, since high effort predicts churn.
- **[First-contact resolution](https://www.ringcentral.com/first-call-resolution) (FCR):** the share of issues solved in a single interaction. Low FCR means customers are repeating themselves across channels, usually because agents can’t see prior context.
- **Digital containment:** the share of issues fully resolved in self-service. It shows whether your digital channels deflect work or only delay a call, and it climbs when self-service answers the questions customers actually ask.


To measure, map each metric to the stage it measures so you’re not reading it in a vacuum:


- CSAT and FCR are most relevant at the support stage
- CES sits at purchase and onboarding where friction costs you conversions
- NPS covers the whole relationship
- Containment tells you whether self-service is doing real work or deferring it to another channel


Set a baseline before defining a performance target. Track each metric on a steady cadence against your own history and[customer engagement data](https://www.ringcentral.com/features/customer-engagement-analytics) , because the trend at a single touchpoint tells you more than an industry average does. The right[customer experience software](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/customer-experience-software/) pulls these metrics into one place, so a drop at one stage is visible the week it happens and not the quarter after.


## Why digital customer experience matters


Weak digital customer experience costs you customers when lower-friction alternatives are readily available. The business case shows up in retention and revenue, and the current benchmarks aren’t reassuring. In its[2024 US Customer Experience Index](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2024-us-customer-experience-index/) , Forrester found that customer experience quality in the US fell to its lowest level on record, with 39% of brands declining over the year.


The cost is measurable.[Qualtrics XM Institute’s 2024 global consumer study](https://www.qualtrics.com/articles/customer-experience/trillion-sales-at-risk-2025/) estimated that poor experiences put 6.1% of a company’s revenue at risk. It also found that 38% of bad experiences lead consumers to spend less at an establishment, and another 15% cause them to stop shopping with a brand entirely.


For a digital operation, those losses collect at the touchpoints customers use most, and they are rarely flagged by customers directly. A customer who gives up at a broken chat handoff rarely files a complaint. They leave without a word. For a mid-market or enterprise operation, that quiet attrition is expensive, since winning a replacement customer almost always costs more than keeping the one you lost.


## Digital customer experience examples


Examples of digital experience are the concrete touchpoints a customer moves through online: a self-service help center, a mobile app, live chat, in-app messaging, and automated order updates. Each is a moment where the experience either holds or breaks, and each maps to a metric you can track.


### Self-service examples


Some digital customer experiences run with little human involvement. A customer resets a password through a self-service portal, or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot answers a billing question and hands off to an agent only when the issue gets complex.


These are containment moments: when they work, they lift digital containment and first-contact resolution at once. Others are human-assisted but still digital. A support agent picks up a live chat with the customer’s full history on screen, so the customer never has to repeat their account number or their problem. That continuity is what keeps CES low.


### B2B examples


In a B2B setting, the touchpoints are often higher-stakes. A renewal portal that shows an account’s own usage supports retention and the loyalty score behind it. An onboarding sequence that gets a new team to first value without a call shortens time to value, which is a key onboarding-stage signal.


### The mix is shifting toward self-service


In a[2025 Gartner survey of service leaders](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-27-gartner-survey-finds-self-service-and-live-chat-will-surpass-traditional-channels-as-top-customer-service-technologies-by-2027) , digital-first channels such as self-service and live chat were expected to overtake phone and email as the most valuable customer service technologies by 2027. These support moments are the heart of[digital customer service](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/digital-customer-service/) , and they’re often where a customer’s opinion of the whole brand is set.


## Bring the digital customer experience into a single view


The hardest part of digital customer experience is structural. Channels get added one at a time, each with its own tools and its own data, so no single team owns the full picture of what the customer went through.


The journey map and the metrics only work if one system can see the whole journey. That’s what a contact center platform provides. RingCentral[RingCX](https://www.ringcentral.com/ringcx) is built as an AI-first contact center as a service (CCaaS) that unifies voice and 20+ digital channels in a single agent workspace, so a customer’s experience stays consistent as they move from chat to email to a call.


That single view does real work. Because agents share one record, a customer who switches channels never restarts. Continuity is what holds first-contact resolution up and CES down.


[Intelligent virtual agents](https://www.ringcentral.com/ringcx/intelligent-virtual-agent) handle routine digital touchpoints like status checks and password resets. That raises digital containment and frees agents for the cases that need a person. Engagement analytics show where in the journey customers disengage, so the digital-experience metrics are anchored to specific journey stages and every performance decline can be attributed to a specific touchpoint.


The result is unified measurement and the delivery on one platform. Agentic tools are widening what that looks like, and the role of[AI in customer experience](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/ai-customer-experience/) is growing from simple deflection toward full resolution.


## Turn digital customer experience into a measurable program


Digital customer experience stops being vague the moment you treat it as a program. Define what it means for your customers, map the journey they actually take, measure the moments that matter, and fix the highest-friction touchpoints before you add anything new.


If you do one thing first, map a single high-volume journey end to end and mark where customers drop off. That’s usually where the fastest gains sit, and it tells you which touchpoint to rebuild first.

## Digital customer experience FAQs


### What are examples of digital experience?


Examples of digital experience include self-service help centers, mobile apps, live chat, chatbots, in-app messaging, automated order and shipping updates, and account portals.


Each is a point where a customer interacts with your brand through a screen rather than a person. The strongest ones carry the customer’s context from one channel to the next, so nothing has to be repeated.


### What is CX vs. CRM?


Customer experience (CX) is how a customer perceives every interaction with your brand, while a[customer relationship management (CRM) platform](https://www.ringcentral.com/us/en/blog/customer-service-software-platform/) is the software that stores customer data and tracks those interactions. CX is the outcome you’re trying to shape, and the CRM platform is one of the systems you use to shape it.


A strong CRM platform supports good experience, but it doesn’t guarantee it, because the experience is what the customer actually feels.


### What are the 5 C’s of customer experience?


The 5 C’s of customer experience are a shorthand some teams use for the pillars of a strong experience. A commonly cited version is:


1. Consistency
2. Convenience
3. Communication
4. Customization
5. Culture


In practice that means being predictable across channels, low-effort to interact with, clear in your messaging, relevant to the individual, and backed by a company culture that puts customers first. Frameworks vary by source, so treat the five as a prompt for what to prioritize rather than a fixed checklist.
